import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Define a specific order for customer age groups for better visualization
age_group_order = ['18-24', '25-34', '35-44', '45-54', '55+']
df['customer_age_group'] = pd.Categorical(df['customer_age_group'], categories=age_group_order, ordered=True)

# Aggregate total sales by product and customer age group
# Unstack to prepare for a stacked bar chart: products as index, age groups as columns
sales_by_product_age = df.groupby(['product', 'customer_age_group'])['total'].sum().unstack()

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Plotting the stacked bar chart
# Use seaborn's color palette
sales_by_product_age.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=plt.gca(), cmap='viridis')

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Customer Age Group', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Customize the legend
plt.legend(title='Customer Age Group', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
